title.narrative: Activity under preparation Climate Mobility and Resilience in the Horn of Africa (CLIMHoA)

description.narrative: The overall objective of the Action is to reduce the impact of climate change, hazards, environmental degradation, and correlated stressors on forcibly displaced persons, migrants and host communities in the Greater Horn of Africa. This Action will support forcibly displaced populations (refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons (IDPs)) as well as migrants (i.e. persons who move away from their place of usual residence, whether within their country or across an international border, temporarily or permanently), with a specific focus on those moving at intra-regional level. It will also support host communities. The concept of «mobility» in the context of climate change and environmental degradation will also be used to encompass the full spectrum of movements.The Action¿s approach is to design area-based interventions targeting forcibly displaced persons and migrants as a whole ¿ although diverse - group of beneficiaries, specifically people who live in areas already affected by and at risk of climate mobility. The programme will focus its interventions on: - addressing the root causes of forced displacement and irregular migration in the context of climate change and environmental degradation by supporting sustainable initiatives and strategies that promote anticipatory action, disaster risk reduction and climate resilience and adaptation; - providing assistance and promoting inclusion of forcibly displaced, migrants and host communities, seeking resilience with durable solutions against climate impacts; and promoting research, data collection and analysis as well as knowledge-sharing. Three specific objectives have been formulated: Anticipatory action, disaster risk management and reliable data-driven early warning systems are strengthened at regional and national levels and in areas affected by climate risks and mobility. The planning and implementation of conflict-sensitive natural resources management in areas impacted by climate mobility is improved. Protection, resilience, and self-reliance mechanisms for the forcibly displaced, migrants and their host communities towards climate impacts are strengthened. Based on a tailored and area-based approach, the Action addresses different crisis scenarios, ranging from environmentally fragile environments affected by or at risk of human mobility due to climate change, environmental degradation or natural hazards to building longer term resilience at the regional, national, local, and community level. The Action is implemented with a regional approach, covering the Horn of Africa, and implemented in up to four countries, as countries share correlated pressures due to the complex interplay of climate change, environmental degradation, conflict, forced displacement and intra-regional migration.
